#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <chrono>
#include <random>
#include <omp.h>
#include "kernels.h"
#include "reference.h"

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <vector size> <number of time steps>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }

  // assume each vector element contains two 4-bit quantized numbers
  const long vector_size = atol(argv[1]);
  const int time_step = atoi(argv[2]);

  int64_t size = vector_size * 2;
  int64_t size_bytes = size * sizeof(float);

  float *g = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *p = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *p_ref = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *m_qscale = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *v_qscale = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  int8_t *m = (int8_t*) malloc (vector_size);
  int8_t *v = (int8_t*) malloc (vector_size);
  float *r = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);

  std::mt19937 gen(19937);
  std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dist(0, 1);
  for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    m_qscale[i] = dist(gen);
    v_qscale[i] = dist(gen);
    g[i] = dist(gen);
    r[i] = p[i] = p_ref[i] = dist(gen);
  }

  for (int64_t i = 0; i < vector_size; i++) {
    m[i] = 256 * dist(gen);
    v[i] = 256 * dist(gen);
  }

  #pragma omp target data map(to: m_qscale[0:size], v_qscale[0:size], \
                                  g[0:size], p[0:size],\
                                  m[0:vector_size], v[0:vector_size])
  {
    const int threadsPerBlock = 64; // fixed at 64
    const int blocksPerGrid = (vector_size+threadsPerBlock-1) / threadsPerBlock;
    const int numTeams = blocksPerGrid;
    const int numThreads = threadsPerBlock;

    // default constants
    const float lr = 1e-3f;
    const float weight_decay = 1e-2f;
    const float beta1 = 0.9f;
    const float beta2 = 0.999f;
    const float eps = 1e-8f;
    const float resid_beta1 = 1.0f - beta1;
    const float resid_beta2 = 1.0f - beta2;
    const float weight_decay_update = 1.0f - lr * weight_decay;

    for (int step = 1; step <= time_step; step++) {

      const float correction1 = 1.0f - powf(beta1, step);
      const float correction2_sqrt = sqrtf(1.0f - powf(beta2, step));
      const float step_size = lr / correction1;

      fused_4bit_kernel<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                numTeams,
                numThreads,
                p,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);

      reference<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                blocksPerGrid,
                p_ref,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);
    }

    #pragma omp target update from (p[0:size]) 

    float absmax_error = 0;
    for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
      absmax_error = fmaxf(absmax_error, fabsf(p[i] - p_ref[i]));
    }
    printf("Absolute maximum error: %f\n", absmax_error);
    printf("%s\n", absmax_error > 1e-3f ? "FAIL" : "PASS");

    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    for (int step = 1; step <= time_step; step++) {

      const float correction1 = 1.0f - powf(beta1, step);
      const float correction2_sqrt = sqrtf(1.0f - powf(beta2, step));
      const float step_size = lr / correction1;

      fused_4bit_kernel<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                numTeams,
                numThreads,
                p,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);
    }
    auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
    printf("Average kernel execution time %f (ms)\n", time * 1e-6f / time_step);
  }

  free(p);
  free(p_ref);
  free(m_qscale);
  free(v_qscale);
  free(m);
  free(v);
  free(g);
  free(r);
  return 0;
}

## Section 1: Grid Size and Block Size

### General Launch-Configuration Rules

The command-line arguments may not be used directly in the launch site and may instead flow through intermediate variables, helper functions, or derived expressions.

- Ignore code after the first target kernel invocation, because only the first execution matters. If the kernel is launched inside a loop, only analyze the first loop iteration that invokes that kernel.
- If the target kernel is templated, only report the first instantiation that is actually executed.

### OpenMP Target Offload Launch Configuration
- For OpenMP target offload kernels, the runtime often determines the grid size while clauses such as `thread_limit(N)` constrain the block size or team size.
- Do not assume the grid size is simply `ceil(total_iterations / thread_limit)`. OpenMP runtimes commonly distribute work through grid-stride style execution, chunking, or implementation-defined scheduling decisions.

## Section 2: FLOP Counting

### Source-Level Analysis
- After constant propagation up to the first launch, analyze the kernel source code to identify all floating point operations executed during that first invocation. Account for the number of launched threads, loop iterations, and warp divergence regions when scaling the total FLOP counts.
- Preprocessor macros from <compile_commands> may affect control flow and floating point work, so include their impact in your analysis.
- Code comments may incorrectly state the number of FLOPs, so do not trust them; calculate the counts yourself.
- Unary negation of a float or double (for example -x) DOES count as a floating point operation.
- Other floating point datatypes such as FP8 should not be counted as FP16, FP32, or FP64 FLOPs.

### Counting Compiler-Generated FP16 and FP32 Instructions
- Count compiler-generated arithmetic instructions if they execute, even when they originate from helper routines, lowered math-library calls, constant materialization, or implementation details rather than explicit source-level arithmetic.
- The compiler may insert packed FP16 instructions such as HFMA2 / HFMA2_32I for constant or zero materialization on some GPU architectures instead of using MOV-family instructions. If these execute, count them as real FP16 arithmetic in the final estimate: each HFMA2 contributes 4 FP16 FLOPs, but this behavior is architecture- and ptxas-dependent, so infer it conservatively when SASS is unavailable.
- Packed FP16 fused multiply-add instructions contribute multiple FP16 FLOPs per instruction. Lower-precision helper instructions used to implement higher-precision or transcendental operations still count toward the precision at which they execute.
- When SASS is available, count the arithmetic instructions on the taken execution path and scale by how many times that path executes. When SASS is not available, acknowledge that source-only counting may under-estimate lowered helper work and provide the best defensible estimate from the source.
- Compilers may also eliminate common subexpressions or reuse previously computed values, which can reduce the true FLOP count. Use the source and SASS together to avoid over-counting optimized-away work.

### Counting FLOPs from Transcendental and Math Library Functions

## Section 3: DRAM Read and Write Byte Counting

### General Principles
- Estimate DRAM bytes read and DRAM bytes written for the same first invocation of the kernel.
- Count only memory traffic attributable to that invocation, not later kernel launches, host-device transfers, or deferred effects outside the invocation being analyzed.
- Although the source may show many reads and writes, the compiler may optimize, combine, or eliminate some of them, so reason carefully from the executed source path when estimating actual global-memory traffic.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.
- For writes, only count the bytes that go beyond the L2 cache and actually reach DRAM when estimating dram_bytes_written_count. Consider the L2 cache size from <gpu_roofline_specs> together with the amount of store traffic to estimate whether written data fits in cache or spills through to DRAM.
- In many cases, if all the writes fit in the L2 cache, then dram_bytes_written_count will be zero, even if the source code shows many store instructions. Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.

### Distinguishing Unique Footprint from Total Traffic
- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.
- For DRAM read estimation: if the unique read footprint (distinct cache lines touched) fits in L2, then after the first compulsory miss, subsequent reads of the same addresses in inner-loop iterations will hit in cache. In this case, DRAM bytes read ≈ unique footprint, not total_loads × element_size.
- For DRAM write estimation: if the unique write footprint fits in L2, then repeated stores to the same addresses will overwrite the same cache lines without eviction, and DRAM bytes written ≈ 0 during the kernel (the dirty lines remain in L2 until a later eviction event).
- Always compute both the unique footprint and the total traffic, then use the L2 cache size to determine which estimate is appropriate.

### Stencil and Streaming Access Patterns
- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.
- When the working set is much larger than L2, account for the possibility of cache-line eviction and refetch rather than assuming perfect reuse.
- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

template <typename T, int block_size>
void reference (
    const int grid_size,
    T* __restrict__ p,
    const T* __restrict__ g,
    T* __restrict__ exp_qscale,// m
    T* __restrict__ sq_qscale, // v
    int8_t* __restrict__ exp,
    int8_t* __restrict__ sq,
    const float beta1,
    const float beta2,
    const float lr,
    const float weight_decay,
    const float eps,
    const float step,
    const int64_t total_size,
    const float correction1,
    const float correction2_sqrt,
    const float step_size,
    const float weight_decay_update,
    const float resid_beta1,
    const float resid_beta2)
{
  for (int block_id = 0; block_id < grid_size; block_id++) {  
    float absmax_exp = 0;
    float absmax_sq = 0;
    float local_exp_left[block_size];
    float local_sq_left[block_size];
    float local_exp_right[block_size];
    float local_sq_right[block_size];
    for (int thread_id = 0; thread_id < block_size; thread_id++) {
      int64_t global_id = (int64_t)block_id * block_size + thread_id;
      if (global_id >= total_size) break;
      const int8_t exp_full = exp[global_id];
      const int8_t sq_full = sq[global_id];

      float2 p2 = reinterpret_cast<float2*>(p)[global_id];
      const float2 g2 = reinterpret_cast<const float2*>(g)[global_id];

      // left side processing -------------------------------------
      const int8_t exp_left_index = exp_full & _bitmask;
      const int8_t sq_left_index = sq_full & _bitmask;

      //decoupled weight decay
      p2.x = p2.x * weight_decay_update;

      // left exp and sq updates
      float exp_avg_qscale = exp_qscale[block_id];

      float exp_left = exp_qmap_[exp_left_index] * exp_avg_qscale;
      exp_left = beta1 * exp_left + resid_beta1 * g2.x;

      float sq_left = sq_qmap_[sq_left_index] * sq_qscale[block_id];
      sq_left = beta2 * sq_left + resid_beta2 * (g2.x * g2.x);

      // param update
      p[global_id*2] = p2.x - (step_size * (exp_left/(sqrtf(sq_left) / correction2_sqrt + eps)));

      // right side processing -------------------------------

      const int8_t exp_right_index = (exp_full >> 4) & _bitmask;
      const int8_t sq_right_index = (sq_full >> 4) & _bitmask;

      //decoupled weight decay, right side
      p2.y = p2.y * weight_decay_update;

      float exp_right = exp_qmap_[exp_right_index] * exp_avg_qscale;
      exp_right = beta1 * exp_right + resid_beta1 * g2.y;

      float sq_right = sq_qmap_[sq_right_index] * sq_qscale[block_id];
      sq_right = beta2 * sq_right + resid_beta2 * (g2.y * g2.y);

      // param update
      p[global_id*2+1] = p2.y - (step_size * (exp_right/(sqrtf(sq_right) / correction2_sqrt + eps)));

      // prepare quantization info - update absmax scales
      float local_absmax_exp = fmaxf(exp_left, exp_right);
      float local_absmax_sq = fmaxf(sq_left, sq_right);

      local_exp_left[thread_id] = exp_left;
      local_exp_right[thread_id] = exp_right;
      local_sq_left[thread_id] = sq_left;
      local_sq_right[thread_id] = sq_right;

      // determine absmax for exp
      absmax_exp = fmaxf(absmax_exp, local_absmax_exp);

      // same for sq
      absmax_sq = fmaxf(absmax_sq, local_absmax_sq);
    }

    exp_qscale[block_id] = absmax_exp;
    sq_qscale[block_id] = absmax_sq;

    for (int thread_id = 0; thread_id < block_size; thread_id++) {
      int64_t global_id = (int64_t)block_id * block_size + thread_id;
      if (global_id >= total_size) break;

      int8_t local_packed_exp = 0;
      int8_t local_packed_sq = 0;

      // quantize and pack
      const int8_t q_exp_left = (int8_t)q_mapping (exp_qmap_, exp_qmidpt_, (float)local_exp_left[thread_id] / absmax_exp);
      const int8_t q_sq_left = (int8_t)q_mapping (sq_qmap_, sq_qmidpt_, (float)local_sq_left[thread_id] / absmax_sq);
      local_packed_exp |= (q_exp_left & _bitmask);
      local_packed_sq |= (q_sq_left & _bitmask);

      const int8_t q_exp_right = (int8_t)q_mapping (exp_qmap_, exp_qmidpt_, (float)local_exp_right[thread_id] / absmax_exp);

      local_packed_exp |= (q_exp_right & _right_pack_bitmask);

      // store updated exp and sq
      exp[global_id] = local_packed_exp;
      sq[global_id] = local_packed_sq;
    }
  }
}

inline float q_mapping(const float* __restrict__ qmap,
                       const float* __restrict__ qmidpt,

#include <math.h>
#include <chrono>

#include <omp.h>
#include "kernels.h"
#include "reference.h"

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <vector size> <number of time steps>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }

  // assume each vector element contains two 4-bit quantized numbers
  const long vector_size = atol(argv[1]);
  const int time_step = atoi(argv[2]);

  int64_t size = vector_size * 2;
  int64_t size_bytes = size * sizeof(float);

  float *g = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *p = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *p_ref = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *m_qscale = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *v_qscale = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  int8_t *m = (int8_t*) malloc (vector_size);
  int8_t *v = (int8_t*) malloc (vector_size);
  float *r = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);

  std::mt19937 gen(19937);
  std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dist(0, 1);
  for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    m_qscale[i] = dist(gen);
    v_qscale[i] = dist(gen);
    g[i] = dist(gen);
    r[i] = p[i] = p_ref[i] = dist(gen);
  }

  for (int64_t i = 0; i < vector_size; i++) {
    m[i] = 256 * dist(gen);
    v[i] = 256 * dist(gen);
  }

  #pragma omp target data map(to: m_qscale[0:size], v_qscale[0:size], \
                                  g[0:size], p[0:size],\
                                  m[0:vector_size], v[0:vector_size])
  {
    const int threadsPerBlock = 64; // fixed at 64
    const int blocksPerGrid = (vector_size+threadsPerBlock-1) / threadsPerBlock;
    const int numTeams = blocksPerGrid;
    const int numThreads = threadsPerBlock;

    // default constants
    const float lr = 1e-3f;
    const float weight_decay = 1e-2f;
    const float beta1 = 0.9f;
    const float beta2 = 0.999f;
    const float eps = 1e-8f;
    const float resid_beta1 = 1.0f - beta1;
    const float resid_beta2 = 1.0f - beta2;
    const float weight_decay_update = 1.0f - lr * weight_decay;

    for (int step = 1; step <= time_step; step++) {

      const float correction1 = 1.0f - powf(beta1, step);
      const float correction2_sqrt = sqrtf(1.0f - powf(beta2, step));
      const float step_size = lr / correction1;

      fused_4bit_kernel<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                numTeams,
                numThreads,
                p,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);

      reference<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                blocksPerGrid,
                p_ref,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);
    }

    #pragma omp target update from (p[0:size]) 

    float absmax_error = 0;
    for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
      absmax_error = fmaxf(absmax_error, fabsf(p[i] - p_ref[i]));
    }
    printf("Absolute maximum error: %f\n", absmax_error);
    printf("%s\n", absmax_error > 1e-3f ? "FAIL" : "PASS");

    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    for (int step = 1; step <= time_step; step++) {

      const float correction1 = 1.0f - powf(beta1, step);
      const float correction2_sqrt = sqrtf(1.0f - powf(beta2, step));
      const float step_size = lr / correction1;

      fused_4bit_kernel<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                numTeams,
                numThreads,
                p,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);
    }
    auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
    printf("Average kernel execution time %f (ms)\n", time * 1e-6f / time_step);
  }

  free(p);
  free(p_ref);
  free(m_qscale);
  free(v_qscale);
  free(m);
  free(v);
  free(g);
  free(r);

### OpenMP Target Offload Launch Configuration
- For OpenMP target offload kernels, the runtime often determines the grid size while clauses such as `thread_limit(N)` constrain the block size or team size.
- Do not assume the grid size is simply `ceil(total_iterations / thread_limit)`. OpenMP runtimes commonly distribute work through grid-stride style execution, chunking, or implementation-defined scheduling decisions.

## Section 2: FLOP Counting

### Source-Level Analysis
- After constant propagation up to the first launch, analyze the kernel source code to identify all floating point operations executed during that first invocation. Account for the number of launched threads, loop iterations, and warp divergence regions when scaling the total FLOP counts.
- Preprocessor macros from <compile_commands> may affect control flow and floating point work, so include their impact in your analysis.
- Code comments may incorrectly state the number of FLOPs, so do not trust them; calculate the counts yourself.
- Unary negation of a float or double (for example -x) DOES count as a floating point operation.

- Count compiler-generated arithmetic instructions if they execute, even when they originate from helper routines, lowered math-library calls, constant materialization, or implementation details rather than explicit source-level arithmetic.

## Section 3: DRAM Read and Write Byte Counting

### General Principles
- Estimate DRAM bytes read and DRAM bytes written for the same first invocation of the kernel.

- Although the source may show many reads and writes, the compiler may optimize, combine, or eliminate some of them, so reason carefully from the executed source path when estimating actual global-memory traffic.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.
- For writes, only count the bytes that go beyond the L2 cache and actually reach DRAM when estimating dram_bytes_written_count. Consider the L2 cache size from <gpu_roofline_specs> together with the amount of store traffic to estimate whether written data fits in cache or spills through to DRAM.
- In many cases, if all the writes fit in the L2 cache, then dram_bytes_written_count will be zero, even if the source code shows many store instructions. Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.

### Distinguishing Unique Footprint from Total Traffic
- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.
- For DRAM read estimation: if the unique read footprint (distinct cache lines touched) fits in L2, then after the first compulsory miss, subsequent reads of the same addresses in inner-loop iterations will hit in cache. In this case, DRAM bytes read ≈ unique footprint, not total_loads × element_size.
- For DRAM write estimation: if the unique write footprint fits in L2, then repeated stores to the same addresses will overwrite the same cache lines without eviction, and DRAM bytes written ≈ 0 during the kernel (the dirty lines remain in L2 until a later eviction event).
- Always compute both the unique footprint and the total traffic, then use the L2 cache size to determine which estimate is appropriate.

### Stencil and Streaming Access Patterns
- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.
- When the working set is much larger than L2, account for the possibility of cache-line eviction and refetch rather than assuming perfect reuse.
- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

template <typename T, int block_size>
void reference (
    const int grid_size,
    T* __restrict__ p,
    const T* __restrict__ g,
    T* __restrict__ exp_qscale,// m
    T* __restrict__ sq_qscale, // v
    int8_t* __restrict__ exp,
    int8_t* __restrict__ sq,
    const float beta1,
    const float beta2,
    const float lr,
    const float weight_decay,
    const float eps,
    const float step,
    const int64_t total_size,
    const float correction1,
    const float correction2_sqrt,
    const float step_size,
    const float weight_decay_update,
    const float resid_beta1,
    const float resid_beta2)
{
  for (int block_id = 0; block_id < grid_size; block_id++) {  
    float absmax_exp = 0;
    float absmax_sq = 0;
    float local_exp_left[block_size];
    float local_sq_left[block_size];
    float local_exp_right[block_size];
    float local_sq_right[block_size];
    for (int thread_id = 0; thread_id < block_size; thread_id++) {
      int64_t global_id = (int64_t)block_id * block_size + thread_id;
      if (global_id >= total_size) break;
      const int8_t exp_full = exp[global_id];
      const int8_t sq_full = sq[global_id];

      float2 p2 = reinterpret_cast<float2*>(p)[global_id];
      const float2 g2 = reinterpret_cast<const float2*>(g)[global_id];

      // left side processing -------------------------------------
      const int8_t exp_left_index = exp_full & _bitmask;
      const int8_t sq_left_index = sq_full & _bitmask;

      //decoupled weight decay
      p2.x = p2.x * weight_decay_update;

      // left exp and sq updates
      float exp_avg_qscale = exp_qscale[block_id];

      float exp_left = exp_qmap_[exp_left_index] * exp_avg_qscale;
      exp_left = beta1 * exp_left + resid_beta1 * g2.x;

      float sq_left = sq_qmap_[sq_left_index] * sq_qscale[block_id];
      sq_left = beta2 * sq_left + resid_beta2 * (g2.x * g2.x);

      // param update

      const int8_t sq_right_index = (sq_full >> 4) & _bitmask;

      local_sq_left[thread_id] = sq_left;
      local_sq_right[thread_id] = sq_right;

      absmax_exp = fmaxf(absmax_exp, local_absmax_exp);

      // same for sq
      absmax_sq = fmaxf(absmax_sq, local_absmax_sq);
    }

    exp_qscale[block_id] = absmax_exp;
    sq_qscale[block_id] = absmax_sq;

    for (int thread_id = 0; thread_id < block_size; thread_id++) {

// binary search for quantization
inline float q_mapping(const float* __restrict__ qmap,
                       const float* __restrict__ qmidpt,
                       float x)
{
    // 4 bit range
    int low = 0;
    int high = 15;

    if (x <= qmap[low]) return low;
    if (qmap[high] <=x) return high;

    // replace with for loop?
    while (low < high) {
        int mid = (low + high) >> 1;
        if (qmap[mid] <= x)
        {
            low = mid + 1;
        }
        else
        {
            high = mid;
        }
    }
    return (qmidpt[low-1] < x) ? low : low-1;
}

template <typename T, int block_size>
void fused_4bit_kernel (
    const int numTeams,
    const int numThreads,
    T* __restrict__ p,
    const T* __restrict__ g,
    T* __restrict__ exp_qscale,// m
    T* __restrict__ sq_qscale, // v
    int8_t* __restrict__ exp,
    int8_t* __restrict__ sq,
    const float beta1,
    const float beta2,
    const float lr,
    const float weight_decay,
    const float eps,
    const float step,
    const int64_t total_size,
    const float correction1,
    const float correction2_sqrt,
    const float step_size,
    const float weight_decay_update,
    const float resid_beta1,
    const float resid_beta2)
{
  #pragma omp target teams distribute num_teams(numTeams)
  for (int block_id = 0; block_id < numTeams; block_id++) {  
    float absmax_exp = 0;
    float absmax_sq = 0;
    float local_exp_left[block_size];
    float local_sq_left[block_size];
    float local_exp_right[block_size];
    float local_sq_right[block_size];
    #pragma omp parallel for reduction(max:absmax_sq, absmax_exp) num_threads(numThreads)
    for (int thread_id = 0; thread_id < block_size; thread_id++) {
      int64_t global_id = (int64_t)block_id * block_size + thread_id;
      if (global_id < total_size) {
        const int8_t exp_full = exp[global_id];
        const int8_t sq_full = sq[global_id];

        float2 p2 = reinterpret_cast<float2*>(p)[global_id];
        const float2 g2 = reinterpret_cast<const float2*>(g)[global_id];

        // left side processing -------------------------------------
        const int8_t exp_left_index = exp_full & _bitmask;
        const int8_t sq_left_index = sq_full & _bitmask;

        //decoupled weight decay
        p2.x = p2.x * weight_decay_update;

        // left exp and sq updates
        float exp_avg_qscale = exp_qscale[block_id];

        float exp_left = _exp_qmap[exp_left_index] * exp_avg_qscale;
        exp_left = beta1 * exp_left + resid_beta1 * g2.x;

        float sq_left = _sq_qmap[sq_left_index] * sq_qscale[block_id];
        sq_left = beta2 * sq_left + resid_beta2 * (g2.x * g2.x);

        // param update
        p[global_id*2] = p2.x - (step_size * (exp_left/(sqrtf(sq_left) / correction2_sqrt + eps)));

        // right side processing -------------------------------

        const int8_t exp_right_index = (exp_full >> 4) & _bitmask;
        const int8_t sq_right_index = (sq_full >> 4) & _bitmask;

        //decoupled weight decay, right side
        p2.y = p2.y * weight_decay_update;

        float exp_right = _exp_qmap[exp_right_index] * exp_avg_qscale;
        exp_right = beta1 * exp_right + resid_beta1 * g2.y;

        float sq_right = _sq_qmap[sq_right_index] * sq_qscale[block_id];
        sq_right = beta2 * sq_right + resid_beta2 * (g2.y * g2.y);

        // param update
        p[global_id*2+1] = p2.y - (step_size * (exp_right/(sqrtf(sq_right) / correction2_sqrt + eps)));

        // prepare quantization info - update absmax scales
        float local_absmax_exp = fmaxf(exp_left, exp_right);
        float local_absmax_sq = fmaxf(sq_left, sq_right);

        local_exp_left[thread_id] = exp_left;
        local_exp_right[thread_id] = exp_right;
        local_sq_left[thread_id] = sq_left;
        local_sq_right[thread_id] = sq_right;

        // determine absmax for exp
        absmax_exp = fmaxf(absmax_exp, local_absmax_exp);

        // same for sq
        absmax_sq = fmaxf(absmax_sq, local_absmax_sq);
      }
    }

    exp_qscale[block_id] = absmax_exp;
    sq_qscale[block_id] = absmax_sq;

    #pragma omp parallel for num_threads(numThreads)
    for (int thread_id = 0; thread_id < block_size; thread_id++) {
      int64_t global_id = (int64_t)block_id * block_size + thread_id;
      if (global_id < total_size) {

        int8_t local_packed_exp = 0;
        int8_t local_packed_sq = 0;

        // quantize and pack
        const int8_t q_exp_left = (int8_t)q_mapping (_exp_qmap, _exp_qmidpt, (float)local_exp_left[thread_id] / absmax_exp);
        const int8_t q_sq_left = (int8_t)q_mapping (_sq_qmap, _sq_qmidpt, (float)local_sq_left[thread_id] / absmax_sq);
        local_packed_exp |= (q_exp_left & _bitmask);
        local_packed_sq |= (q_sq_left & _bitmask);

        const int8_t q_exp_right = (int8_t)q_mapping (_exp_qmap, _exp_qmidpt, (float)local_exp_right[thread_id] / absmax_exp);
        const int8_t q_sq_right = (int8_t)q_mapping (_sq_qmap, _sq_qmidpt, (float)local_sq_right[thread_id] / absmax_sq);
        local_packed_exp |= (q_exp_right & _right_pack_bitmask);
        local_packed_sq |= (q_sq_right & _right_pack_bitmask);

        // store updated exp and sq
        exp[global_id] = local_packed_exp;
        sq[global_id] = local_packed_sq;
      }
    }
  }
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <chrono>
#include <random>
#include <omp.h>
#include "kernels.h"
#include "reference.h"

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <vector size> <number of time steps>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }

  // assume each vector element contains two 4-bit quantized numbers
  const long vector_size = atol(argv[1]);
  const int time_step = atoi(argv[2]);

  int64_t size = vector_size * 2;
  int64_t size_bytes = size * sizeof(float);

  float *g = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *p = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *p_ref = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *m_qscale = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *v_qscale = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  int8_t *m = (int8_t*) malloc (vector_size);
  int8_t *v = (int8_t*) malloc (vector_size);
  float *r = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);

  std::mt19937 gen(19937);
  std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dist(0, 1);
  for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    m_qscale[i] = dist(gen);
    v_qscale[i] = dist(gen);
    g[i] = dist(gen);
    r[i] = p[i] = p_ref[i] = dist(gen);
  }

  for (int64_t i = 0; i < vector_size; i++) {
    m[i] = 256 * dist(gen);
    v[i] = 256 * dist(gen);
  }

  #pragma omp target data map(to: m_qscale[0:size], v_qscale[0:size], \
                                  g[0:size], p[0:size],\
                                  m[0:vector_size], v[0:vector_size])
  {
    const int threadsPerBlock = 64; // fixed at 64
    const int blocksPerGrid = (vector_size+threadsPerBlock-1) / threadsPerBlock;
    const int numTeams = blocksPerGrid;
    const int numThreads = threadsPerBlock;

    // default constants
    const float lr = 1e-3f;
    const float weight_decay = 1e-2f;
    const float beta1 = 0.9f;
    const float beta2 = 0.999f;
    const float eps = 1e-8f;
    const float resid_beta1 = 1.0f - beta1;
    const float resid_beta2 = 1.0f - beta2;
    const float weight_decay_update = 1.0f - lr * weight_decay;

    for (int step = 1; step <= time_step; step++) {

      const float correction1 = 1.0f - powf(beta1, step);
      const float correction2_sqrt = sqrtf(1.0f - powf(beta2, step));
      const float step_size = lr / correction1;

      fused_4bit_kernel<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                numTeams,
                numThreads,
                p,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);

      reference<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                blocksPerGrid,
                p_ref,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);
    }

    #pragma omp target update from (p[0:size]) 

    float absmax_error = 0;
    for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
      absmax_error = fmaxf(absmax_error, fabsf(p[i] - p_ref[i]));
    }
    printf("Absolute maximum error: %f\n", absmax_error);
    printf("%s\n", absmax_error > 1e-3f ? "FAIL" : "PASS");

    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    for (int step = 1; step <= time_step; step++) {

      const float correction1 = 1.0f - powf(beta1, step);
      const float correction2_sqrt = sqrtf(1.0f - powf(beta2, step));
      const float step_size = lr / correction1;

      fused_4bit_kernel<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                numTeams,
                numThreads,
                p,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);
    }
    auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
    printf("Average kernel execution time %f (ms)\n", time * 1e-6f / time_step);
  }

  free(p);
  free(p_ref);
  free(m_qscale);
  free(v_qscale);
  free(m);
  free(v);
  free(g);
  free(r);
  return 0;
}

- After constant propagation up to the first launch, analyze the kernel source code to identify all floating point operations executed during that first invocation. Account for the number of launched threads, loop iterations, and warp divergence regions when scaling the total FLOP counts.
- Preprocessor macros from <compile_commands> may affect control flow and floating point work, so include their impact in your analysis.
- Code comments may incorrectly state the number of FLOPs, so do not trust them; calculate the counts yourself.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.

- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.

- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. static const uint8_t _bitmask = 15;
static const uint8_t _right_pack_bitmask = _bitmask << 4;

struct float2 {
  float x;
  float y;
};

static const float _exp_qmap [] = {
                -0.8875,
                -0.6625,

                0.8875,
                1.0000,
};

static const float _exp_qmidpt [] = {

            -0.775,
            -0.55,

            0.00275,

};

static const float _sq_qmap [] = {
                0.0625,

                0.4375,
                0.5000,

                0.7500,
                0.8125,

                0.9375,
                1.0000,
};

static const float _sq_qmidpt [] = {
            0.09375,
            0.15625,
            0.21875,

// binary search for quantization
inline float q_mapping(const float* __restrict__ qmap,
                       const float* __restrict__ qmidpt,
                       float x)
{
    // 4 bit range
    int low = 0;
    int high = 15;

    if (x <= qmap[low]) return low;
    if (qmap[high] <=x) return high;

    // replace with for loop?
    while (low < high) {
        int mid = (low + high) >> 1;
        if (qmap[mid] <= x)
        {
            low = mid + 1;
        }
        else
        {
            high = mid;
        }
    }
    return (qmidpt[low-1] < x) ? low : low-1;
}

template <typename T, int block_size>
void fused_4bit_kernel (
    const int numTeams,
    const int numThreads,
    T* __restrict__ p,
    const T* __restrict__ g,
    T* __restrict__ exp_qscale,// m
    T* __restrict__ sq_qscale, // v
    int8_t* __restrict__ exp,
    int8_t* __restrict__ sq,
    const float beta1,
    const float beta2,
    const float lr,
    const float weight_decay,
    const float eps,
    const float step,
    const int64_t total_size,
    const float correction1,
    const float correction2_sqrt,
    const float step_size,
    const float weight_decay_update,
    const float resid_beta1,
    const float resid_beta2)
{
  #pragma omp target teams distribute num_teams(numTeams)
  for (int block_id = 0; block_id < numTeams; block_id++) {  
    float absmax_exp = 0;
    float absmax_sq = 0;
    float local_exp_left[block_size];
    float local_sq_left[block_size];
    float local_exp_right[block_size];
    float local_sq_right[block_size];
    #pragma omp parallel for reduction(max:absmax_sq, absmax_exp) num_threads(numThreads)
    for (int thread_id = 0; thread_id < block_size; thread_id++) {
      int64_t global_id = (int64_t)block_id * block_size + thread_id;
      if (global_id < total_size) {
        const int8_t exp_full = exp[global_id];
        const int8_t sq_full = sq[global_id];

        float2 p2 = reinterpret_cast<float2*>(p)[global_id];
        const float2 g2 = reinterpret_cast<const float2*>(g)[global_id];

        // left side processing -------------------------------------
        const int8_t exp_left_index = exp_full & _bitmask;
        const int8_t sq_left_index = sq_full & _bitmask;

        //decoupled weight decay
        p2.x = p2.x * weight_decay_update;

        // left exp and sq updates
        float exp_avg_qscale = exp_qscale[block_id];

        float exp_left = _exp_qmap[exp_left_index] * exp_avg_qscale;
        exp_left = beta1 * exp_left + resid_beta1 * g2.x;

        float sq_left = _sq_qmap[sq_left_index] * sq_qscale[block_id];
        sq_left = beta2 * sq_left + resid_beta2 * (g2.x * g2.x);

        // param update
        p[global_id*2] = p2.x - (step_size * (exp_left/(sqrtf(sq_left) / correction2_sqrt + eps)));

        // right side processing -------------------------------

        const int8_t exp_right_index = (exp_full >> 4) & _bitmask;
        const int8_t sq_right_index = (sq_full >> 4) & _bitmask;

        //decoupled weight decay, right side
        p2.y = p2.y * weight_decay_update;

        float exp_right = _exp_qmap[exp_right_index] * exp_avg_qscale;
        exp_right = beta1 * exp_right + resid_beta1 * g2.y;

        float sq_right = _sq_qmap[sq_right_index] * sq_qscale[block_id];
        sq_right = beta2 * sq_right + resid_beta2 * (g2.y * g2.y);

        // param update
        p[global_id*2+1] = p2.y - (step_size * (exp_right/(sqrtf(sq_right) / correction2_sqrt + eps)));

        // prepare quantization info - update absmax scales
        float local_absmax_exp = fmaxf(exp_left, exp_right);
        float local_absmax_sq = fmaxf(sq_left, sq_right);

        local_exp_left[thread_id] = exp_left;
        local_exp_right[thread_id] = exp_right;
        local_sq_left[thread_id] = sq_left;
        local_sq_right[thread_id] = sq_right;

        // determine absmax for exp
        absmax_exp = fmaxf(absmax_exp, local_absmax_exp);

        // same for sq
        absmax_sq = fmaxf(absmax_sq, local_absmax_sq);
      }
    }

    exp_qscale[block_id] = absmax_exp;
    sq_qscale[block_id] = absmax_sq;

    #pragma omp parallel for num_threads(numThreads)
    for (int thread_id = 0; thread_id < block_size; thread_id++) {
      int64_t global_id = (int64_t)block_id * block_size + thread_id;
      if (global_id < total_size) {

        int8_t local_packed_exp = 0;
        int8_t local_packed_sq = 0;

        // quantize and pack
        const int8_t q_exp_left = (int8_t)q_mapping (_exp_qmap, _exp_qmidpt, (float)local_exp_left[thread_id] / absmax_exp);
        const int8_t q_sq_left = (int8_t)q_mapping (_sq_qmap, _sq_qmidpt, (float)local_sq_left[thread_id] / absmax_sq);
        local_packed_exp |= (q_exp_left & _bitmask);
        local_packed_sq |= (q_sq_left & _bitmask);

        const int8_t q_exp_right = (int8_t)q_mapping (_exp_qmap, _exp_qmidpt, (float)local_exp_right[thread_id] / absmax_exp);
        const int8_t q_sq_right = (int8_t)q_mapping (_sq_qmap, _sq_qmidpt, (float)local_sq_right[thread_id] / absmax_sq);
        local_packed_exp |= (q_exp_right & _right_pack_bitmask);
        local_packed_sq |= (q_sq_right & _right_pack_bitmask);

        // store updated exp and sq
        exp[global_id] = local_packed_exp;
        sq[global_id] = local_packed_sq;
      }
    }
  }
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <chrono>
#include <random>
#include <omp.h>
#include "kernels.h"
#include "reference.h"

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <vector size> <number of time steps>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }

  // assume each vector element contains two 4-bit quantized numbers
  const long vector_size = atol(argv[1]);
  const int time_step = atoi(argv[2]);

  int64_t size = vector_size * 2;
  int64_t size_bytes = size * sizeof(float);

  float *g = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *p = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *p_ref = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *m_qscale = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  float *v_qscale = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);
  int8_t *m = (int8_t*) malloc (vector_size);
  int8_t *v = (int8_t*) malloc (vector_size);
  float *r = (float*) malloc (size_bytes);

  std::mt19937 gen(19937);
  std::uniform_real_distribution<float> dist(0, 1);
  for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
    m_qscale[i] = dist(gen);
    v_qscale[i] = dist(gen);
    g[i] = dist(gen);
    r[i] = p[i] = p_ref[i] = dist(gen);
  }

  for (int64_t i = 0; i < vector_size; i++) {
    m[i] = 256 * dist(gen);
    v[i] = 256 * dist(gen);
  }

  #pragma omp target data map(to: m_qscale[0:size], v_qscale[0:size], \
                                  g[0:size], p[0:size],\
                                  m[0:vector_size], v[0:vector_size])
  {
    const int threadsPerBlock = 64; // fixed at 64
    const int blocksPerGrid = (vector_size+threadsPerBlock-1) / threadsPerBlock;
    const int numTeams = blocksPerGrid;
    const int numThreads = threadsPerBlock;

    // default constants
    const float lr = 1e-3f;
    const float weight_decay = 1e-2f;
    const float beta1 = 0.9f;
    const float beta2 = 0.999f;
    const float eps = 1e-8f;
    const float resid_beta1 = 1.0f - beta1;
    const float resid_beta2 = 1.0f - beta2;
    const float weight_decay_update = 1.0f - lr * weight_decay;

    for (int step = 1; step <= time_step; step++) {

      const float correction1 = 1.0f - powf(beta1, step);
      const float correction2_sqrt = sqrtf(1.0f - powf(beta2, step));
      const float step_size = lr / correction1;

      fused_4bit_kernel<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                numTeams,
                numThreads,
                p,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);

      reference<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                blocksPerGrid,
                p_ref,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);
    }

    #pragma omp target update from (p[0:size]) 

    float absmax_error = 0;
    for (int64_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
      absmax_error = fmaxf(absmax_error, fabsf(p[i] - p_ref[i]));
    }
    printf("Absolute maximum error: %f\n", absmax_error);
    printf("%s\n", absmax_error > 1e-3f ? "FAIL" : "PASS");

    auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

    for (int step = 1; step <= time_step; step++) {

      const float correction1 = 1.0f - powf(beta1, step);
      const float correction2_sqrt = sqrtf(1.0f - powf(beta2, step));
      const float step_size = lr / correction1;

      fused_4bit_kernel<float, threadsPerBlock>(
                numTeams,
                numThreads,
                p,
                g,
                m_qscale,
                v_qscale,
                m,
                v,
                beta1,
                beta2,
                lr,
                weight_decay,
                eps,
                step,
                vector_size,
                correction1,
                correction2_sqrt,
                step_size,
                weight_decay_update,
                resid_beta1,
                resid_beta2);
    }
    auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
    printf("Average kernel execution time %f (ms)\n", time * 1e-6f / time_step);
  }

  free(p);
  free(p_ref);
  free(m_qscale);
  free(v_qscale);
  free(m);
  free(v);
  free(g);
  free(r);
  return 0;
}

prediction.gridSz_explanation: From the host code: vector_size = 1000000, threadsPerBlock = 64, blocksPerGrid = (1000000 + 64 - 1) / 64 = 15625. The kernel is launched with `num_teams(numTeams)` where numTeams = 15625. The OpenMP runtime maps each team to one CTA, so gridSz.x = 15625.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: The kernel uses `num_threads(numThreads)` where numThreads = 64. However, the OpenMP runtime on NVIDIA GPUs typically rounds up to a warp boundary. Looking at the SASS, the kernel uses warp-level shuffle reductions and shared memory patterns consistent with a block size of 64 threads (2 warps). The block size is 64.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
The kernel has two main phases per team (block): Phase 1 (the compute loop) and Phase 2 (the quantization loop). Each team processes block_size=64 elements (total_size=1000000, all 64 threads active for most blocks).

Phase 1 (per thread, both left and right sides):
For each side (left/right):
- FMUL (g*g): 1
- FMUL (resid_beta2 * g*g): 1 → via FMUL R66,R7 → R0
- FMUL (qmap * qscale): 1
- FFMA (beta2 * sq_left + ...): 1 → FFMA R65,R98,R0
- FMUL (weight_decay_update * p): 1 → FMUL R62,R3
- FMUL (qmap * qscale for exp): 1
- FMUL (beta1 * exp_left): via FMUL R64,R11 → R6
- FFMA (beta1*exp + resid_beta1*g): 1 → FFMA R63,R96,R0
- sqrtf(sq): MUFU.SQRT = 1 FLOP, plus subnormal handling (FMUL for rescale, FSEL)
- Division sqrt/correction2_sqrt: MUFU.RCP + FFMA(-R2,R9,1) + FFMA(R9,R0,R9) + FFMA(R4,R9,RZ) + FFMA(-R2,R0,R4) + FFMA(R9,R8,R0) = 1 RCP + 5 FFMA = 6 FLOPs
- Division exp_left/(sqrt+eps): FADD + MUFU.RCP + FFMA*4 = 1+1+4 = 6 FLOPs
- FFMA for final param update: FFMA(-R67,R4,R100) = 1 FLOP
- FMNMX for absmax: 1

Per side: FMUL*5 + FFMA*3 + MUFU.SQRT*1 + div(sqrt/corr2): 6 + div(exp/(sqrt+eps)): 6 + FADD: 1 + FFMA: 1 + FMNMX: 1 + FMUL(subnormal)*1 + FSEL*1

Let me count from SASS more carefully for one iteration (both left and right):

Left side:
- FMUL R7=R11*R11: 1
- FMUL R0=R66*R7: 1
- MUFU.RCP R9=RCP(R2): 1
- FMUL R6=R64*R11: 1
- FMUL R98=R8*R13: 1
- FFMA R98=R65*R98+R0: 1
- FMUL R7=R98*16M: 1
- MUFU.SQRT R4: 1
- FFMA R0=-R2*R9+1: 1
- FFMA R9=R9*R0+R9: 1
- FMUL R4=R4*0.000244: 1 (conditional, ~never for normal values)
- FFMA R0=R4*R9+RZ: 1
- FMUL R16=R96*R5: 1
- FFMA R8=-R2*R0+R4: 1
- FFMA R16=R63*R16+R6: 1
- FMUL R100=R62*R3: 1
- FFMA R0=R9*R8+R0: 1
- FADD R5=R69+R0: 1
- MUFU.RCP R0=RCP(R5): 1
- FFMA R3=-R5*R0+1: 1
- FFMA R3=R0*R3+R0: 1
- FFMA R4=R16*R3+RZ: 1
- FFMA R0=-R5*R4+R16: 1
- FFMA R4=R3*R0+R4: 1
- FFMA R3=-R67*R4+R100: 1
Left total: ~25 FP32 ops

Right side (similar): ~25 FP32 ops
Plus FMNMX*4 for absmax: 4

Per thread per iteration: ~54 FP32 ops

Phase 2 (quantization, per thread): 4 divisions (MUFU.RCP + 5 FFMA each = 6 each) = 24 FP32 ops, plus binary search comparisons (FSETP) and LDG for qmap lookups. Each q_mapping has ~4 iterations of binary search with FSETP.GTU = ~4 FP32 each × 4 calls = 16. Plus boundary checks ~4 FSETP = 4.

Per thread total ≈ 54 + 24 + 16 + 4 ≈ 98 FP32 ops

Total threads = 15625 * 64 = 1,000,000
Total FP32 ≈ 1,000,000 * 98 ≈ 98,000,000

But let me be more precise. The FSEL counts as FP32 too. Counting SASS carefully for the main loop body (both sides): FMUL×10, FFMA×16, MUFU.RCP×2, MUFU.SQRT×2, FADD×2, FMNMX×4, FSETP×2, FSEL×2 = 40 arithmetic + reductions. For quantization phase: 4 divisions × (MUFU.RCP + 5 FFMA) + 4 binary searches × ~4 FSETP + 4 FSETP boundary. Total per thread ≈ 54 + 24 + 20 = ~98.

Total: 1,000,000 × 98 = 98,000,000

prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: No half-precision floating point operations are present in this kernel. The SASS shows no HFMA2, HMUL2, or HADD2 instructions.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation:
Per thread in Phase 1, the kernel reads:
- exp[global_id]: 1 byte (int8_t)
- sq[global_id]: 1 byte (int8_t)
- p2 (float2): 8 bytes
- g2 (float2): 8 bytes
- exp_qscale[block_id]: 4 bytes (shared across block, 1 read per block)
- sq_qscale[block_id]: 4 bytes (shared across block)
- Two qmap lookups for left: 2×4 = 8 bytes
- exp_qscale[block_id] again for right (cached): 0
- Two qmap lookups for right: 2×4 = 8 bytes

Per thread unique reads: 1+1+8+8+8+8 = 34 bytes, plus per-block: 4+4 = 8 bytes

In Phase 2, the kernel reads from shared memory (local arrays) and does qmap/qmidpt lookups via LDG. Each binary search does ~4 LDG.E reads of 4 bytes from qmap arrays (16 entries each). 4 q_mapping calls × ~4 reads × 4 bytes = 64 bytes, but these are from small constant arrays (16×4=64 bytes each) that will be cached in L1/L2 after first access.

Unique data footprint:
- p array: 1,000,000 × 8 = 8,000,000 bytes
- g array: 1,000,000 × 8 = 8,000,000 bytes
- exp array: 1,000,000 × 1 = 1,000,000 bytes
- sq array: 1,000,000 × 1 = 1,000,000 bytes
- exp_qscale: 15,625 × 4 = 62,500 bytes
- sq_qscale: 15,625 × 4 = 62,500 bytes
- qmap arrays: ~256 bytes (fits in cache)

Total unique read footprint ≈ 18,125,000 bytes. This exceeds L2 (6MB), so most reads go to DRAM. DRAM bytes read ≈ 18,125,000 bytes.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation:
Per thread in Phase 1, the kernel writes:
- p[global_id*2]: 4 bytes (left param update) via STG.E
- p[global_id*2+1]: 4 bytes (right param update) via STG.E
Total: 8 bytes per thread = 8,000,000 bytes for p array

Per block: exp_qscale[block_id] and sq_qscale[block_id]: 4+4 = 8 bytes per block
= 15,625 × 8 = 125,000 bytes

Per thread in Phase 2:
- exp[global_id]: 1 byte (STG.E.U8)
- sq[global_id]: 1 byte (STG.E.U8)
Total: 2 bytes per thread = 2,000,000 bytes

Total unique write footprint: 8,000,000 + 125,000 + 2,000,000 = 10,125,000 bytes.

This exceeds the 6MB L2 cache, so most writes will spill to DRAM. DRAM bytes written ≈ 10,125,000 bytes.

- sq_qmap lookup * sq_qscale (1 mul), beta2 * sq_left (1 mul), resid_beta2 * (g2.x * g2.x) (2 muls), add (1 add) = 4 muls + 1 add = 5 FLOPs
- p2.x * weight_decay_update (1 mul) = 1 FLOP
- param update left: sqrtf(sq_left) (1 FLOP for MUFU), div by correction2_sqrt (1 div), + eps (1 add), exp_left / result (1 div), * step_size (1 mul), p2.x - result (1 sub) = ~6 FLOPs
- Right side: same as left = 4 + 5 + 1 + 6 = 16 FLOPs
- fmaxf operations: fmaxf(exp_left, exp_right) (1), fmaxf(sq_left, sq_right) (1), fmaxf(absmax_exp, local_absmax_exp) (1), fmaxf(absmax_sq, local_absmax_sq) (1) = 4 FLOPs
- Plus reduction max operations across the warp/block

Left side total: 4 + 5 + 1 + 6 = 16 FLOPs
Right side total: 4 + 5 + 1 + 6 = 16 FLOPs
fmaxf: 4 FLOPs
Total per thread first region: ~36 FLOPs

In the SECOND parallel region (quantization):
- Per thread: 4 divisions (local_exp_left/absmax_exp, local_sq_left/absmax_sq, local_exp_right/absmax_exp, local_sq_right/absmax_sq) = 4 FLOPs
- q_mapping involves comparisons with float values (binary search). Each q_mapping call does ~4 iterations of binary search with float comparisons. The comparisons (<=, <) on floats count as FP32 operations (FSETP). Each call: ~2 initial comparisons + ~4 loop iteration comparisons + 1 final comparison ≈ 7 FP32 comparison ops. 4 calls = ~28 FP32 FLOPs from comparisons.

Total per thread second region: 4 + 28 = 32 FLOPs

Total per thread: 36 + 32 = 68 FLOPs
Total: 1000000 * 68 = 68,000,000 FLOPs

However, sqrtf expands to MUFU.SQRT or MUFU.RSQ + FMUL on Ampere, and divisions expand to MUFU.RCP + FMUL sequences. Each division is roughly 2 FP32 ops (RCP + MUL), and sqrt is ~1-2 ops. Let me be more careful:
- 2 sqrtf calls → ~2 FP32 ops each (RSQ + MUL) = 4
- 4 divisions in param update (2 per side: exp_left/denom, correction2_sqrt division) → ~2 each = 8
- 4 divisions in quantization → ~2 each = 8

Adjusting: replace 2 sqrtf (counted as 1 each) with 2 each = +2, replace 6 divs (counted as 1 each) with 2 each = +6. Net adjustment: +8.

Revised: ~76 FLOPs per thread. Total: 1000000 * 76 = 76,000,000.

Given uncertainty in exact compiler lowering, I'll estimate ~68,000,000 based on source-level counting.
metrics_explanations.fp64_flop_explanation: No double-precision floating point operations are performed in this kernel. All arithmetic is done in float (FP32). The only 64-bit type used is int64_t for index calculations, which are integer operations, not FP64.
metrics_explanations.fp16_flop_explanation: No half-precision floating point operations are present in the source code. The compiler may insert a small number of HFMA2 instructions for constant/zero materialization on Ampere, but this is uncertain without SASS. Estimating 0 FP16 FLOPs as a conservative source-level estimate.
metrics_explanations.dram_bytes_read_explanation:
Per thread (1,000,000 active threads total):
- exp[global_id]: 1 byte (int8_t)
- sq[global_id]: 1 byte (int8_t)
- p as float2 (reinterpret_cast<float2*>(p)[global_id]): 8 bytes (2 floats)
- g as float2: 8 bytes (2 floats)
- exp_qscale[block_id]: 4 bytes (shared across block, 1 read per block = 15625 reads)
- sq_qscale[block_id]: 4 bytes (shared across block, 1 read per block = 15625 reads)
- Lookup tables (_exp_qmap, _sq_qmap, _exp_qmidpt, _sq_qmidpt): small constant arrays, likely cached after first access.

Unique read footprint:
- p array: 1000000 * 8 = 8,000,000 bytes
- g array: 1000000 * 8 = 8,000,000 bytes
- exp array: 1000000 * 1 = 1,000,000 bytes
- sq array: 1000000 * 1 = 1,000,000 bytes
- exp_qscale: 15625 * 4 = 62,500 bytes
- sq_qscale: 15625 * 4 = 62,500 bytes
- Lookup tables: ~244 bytes (negligible, cached)

Total unique read footprint: ~18,125,000 bytes ≈ 18.1 MB

The L2 cache is 5 MB, so this data does not fit entirely in L2. Most reads will go to DRAM. The local arrays (local_exp_left, etc.) are in shared memory or local memory within the block. In the second parallel region, the local arrays are re-read from local/shared memory, not DRAM.

DRAM bytes read ≈ 18,125,000 bytes. Rounding to cache line granularity (128 bytes): the data is accessed contiguously, so minimal overhead. Estimate ~18,125,000 bytes.
metrics_explanations.dram_bytes_written_explanation:
Per thread writes:
- p[global_id*2]: 4 bytes (left param update)
- p[global_id*2+1]: 4 bytes (right param update)
- exp[global_id]: 1 byte (quantized)
- sq[global_id]: 1 byte (quantized)
- exp_qscale[block_id]: 4 bytes per block (15625 blocks)
- sq_qscale[block_id]: 4 bytes per block (15625 blocks)

Unique write footprint:
- p array: 1000000 * 8 = 8,000,000 bytes
- exp array: 1000000 * 1 = 1,000,000 bytes
- sq array: 1000000 * 1 = 1,000,000 bytes
- exp_qscale: 15625 * 4 = 62,500 bytes
- sq_qscale: 15625 * 4 = 62,500 bytes

Total unique write footprint: ~10,125,000 bytes ≈ 10.1 MB

The L2 cache is 5 MB. The write footprint exceeds L2, so most writes will spill to DRAM. Additionally, write-allocate policy means each cache line written for the first time may also trigger a read from DRAM, but we only count write traffic here.

The writes to p happen in the first parallel region, and writes to exp/sq happen in the second parallel region. The p writes (8 MB) alone exceed L2, so by the time the second region writes exp/sq, some p lines will have been evicted to DRAM. The total DRAM write traffic should be approximately equal to the unique write footprint: ~10,125,000 bytes.
